places.name: Grand Théâtre de Bordeaux
places.description: Victor Louis's neoclassical masterpiece built 1780. 12 columns carrying Muses and Graces statues, one of France's finest opera house interiors. Grand Staircase was the direct model for Garnier's Paris Opéra.
highlights: Tour de la ville vantage over Place de la Comédie

places.name: La Cité du Vin
places.description: The wine-world equivalent of a Guggenheim: a spiralling bronze-and-glass museum opened 2016. 19 permanent galleries on wine culture. Entry includes one glass of wine on the belvedere terrace, 35m above the Garonne.
highlights: Belvedere at 35m — glass of wine included
Designed by Anouk Legendre + Nicolas Desmazières

places.name: Miroir d'Eau
places.description: The world's largest reflecting pool: 3,450m² of black granite, 2cm of water, misting every 15 minutes. Reflects the 18th-century Place de la Bourse. At dusk, the twin reflections of stone and sky are Bordeaux's most photographed image.
highlights: At dusk: Place de la Bourse doubles in the water

places.name: Darwin Écosystème
places.description: Former military barracks converted into an urban ecosystem: co-working, organic restaurant, skate park, climbing wall, Sunday market, vintage clothing. The coolest address on the Right Bank — everything that Bordeaux wine tourism isn't.
highlights: Darwin bio restaurant with garden terrace

places.name: Quais de la Garonne
places.description: 4.5km of regenerated riverfront on the crescent Garonne bend. Péniches (barge bars), wine merchants, pop-up restaurants on summer pontoons. The quays best explain why Bordeaux earned its UNESCO World Heritage designation in 2007.
highlights: June Fête du Vin — 600 wines free tasting

places.name: Saint-Émilion Village
places.description: Medieval hilltop wine village, 35min from Bordeaux. Entirely UNESCO-listed. Chateau Ausone, Château Pétrus. Underground monolithic church carved from limestone. Macarons invented here in 1620 by Ursuline nuns.
highlights: Underground monolithic church — carved from rock
Château Ausone — Premier Grand Cru Classé A

places.name: Marché des Chartrons
places.description: Sunday morning street market in the historic wine merchants' quarter. Oysters from Arcachon Bay, rillettes, foie gras, Périgord walnuts, local cheeses. Historically the district where Dutch, English and Irish wine traders settled in the 18th century.
highlights: Arcachon oysters shucked to order Sunday 8am
Best natural wine selection in Bordeaux

places.name: Le Chapon Fin
places.description: Bordeaux's most storied restaurant, operating since 1825. Toulouse-Lautrec and Sarah Bernhardt dined here. The Art Nouveau grotto dining room (1901) is classified a historic monument. Nicolas Frion's modern Gironde cuisine.
highlights: Art Nouveau grotto dining room (classified monument)
